risk_note: RV1 (identity module only; no migration, no contract change). FU-APPLE-TOKEN-AFTER-DELETE (notices 6515-6516; D10-966 / D10-968): an Apple refresh token exchanged for an account in deletion was neither stored nor revoked — oauth-login signIn aborts deleting (10007) / deleted (50001) and rolls the login transaction back; reverify byOauth's settlePassed writes nothing for such an account. Basis BR-ID-27 (Sign in with Apple users must be revoked) and BR-ID-28 (user_oauth: revoke the Apple authorization first). Now enqueueDiscardedAppleToken encrypts the token (APPLE_REFRESH_TOKEN_CONTEXT) and writes one existing apple_unbind_revoke job (B1-02zw) in a short transaction of its own, after the rolled-back login / outside the reverify settle; responses unchanged; no user_oauth write. Not enqueued: other 50001, restricted login 10405 no_account (BR-ID-04 detail unchanged), non-Apple providers, no token, reverify mismatch 20005 (D10-968). An enqueue failure keeps the response and logs one warn without the token. Login and reverify services now require the job queue; identity.module injects JOB_QUEUE, which platform.module always provides together with DB (platform.module.ts:112/126). Implementer unit-test fake tokens shortened after gitleaks cn-doc-secret flagged them (no rule change, no bypass). Full verification is the required CI checks (approvals 21; AWS runners off, D10-555).
